sections.value:
**Performance: PASS WITH NOTES** at `516523b6f1d773c9902b597c5b38ccc03e4f9417`.

Light whole-PR cost review against base `8a164b4bf93c30bef427444e115e48871ad0d032`. No added executable launch, store/registry read, periodic worker, retry or timer.

**Admission:** `registration.rs:825-834` checks a claimed ID once per attempt that would mint a new row, after the existing registration-target selection; existing/prebound targets skip it. This is not a new check on every heartbeat or every already-bound registration. Spawn's explicit ID is checked before its existing lookup/launch path; revive retains its existing-row behavior. Valid seat IDs perform an allocation-free ASCII scan bounded by 64 bytes. Refused ID/role/adoption diagnostics escape and take at most 64 output characters before formatting, instead of copying unrestricted raw input. Their existing refusal/audit paths remain, with no new process or read.

**Digest:** checks run only when the existing digest is rendered, over its existing rows, anomalies, requests and held messages. Valid seat/message IDs are bounded by 64/128 bytes; role membership checks use the fixed vocabulary. `Cow::Borrowed` avoids a new allocation on valid direct-render paths. Flagged/anomaly names still become owned strings, as before.

**P182-N001, the invalid fallback is not bounded by the accepted grammar.** `model.rs:80-81` uses `raw.chars().count()` to produce `invalid (N chars)`. Rejecting an overlong field therefore still scans its full raw text and allocates a short placeholder. This applies to stored invalid seat IDs/roles and caller-chosen message/request IDs. The table calls `SeatId::rendered()` once for width and again for the row, so an invalid seat ID incurs two character counts/placeholder allocations there, plus any headline/flagged/anomaly/request/held appearances. Price total work by rendered occurrences and raw invalid-field lengths, not one constant-time check per distinct seat.

The output itself is bounded: table width now uses canonical IDs or short placeholders. A single oversized invalid ID can no longer pad every row to its raw length, removing that prior allocation/output amplification. No delimiter-proportional vector or new malformed-input retry is introduced. The remaining full-text character count is a cost qualification, not a claim that this guard is constant-time.

**Exact-head CI:** [42454424975](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42454424975), successful Rust job `128650303222`, exact upload artifact **13607366481**: **2,215 executed cases passed**, zero failures/errors, five separately skipped. Verified generated-ID corpus/hostile-ID grammar, new-seat admission, HTTP forged-ID/role refusals, closed-role setters, hostile digest-field rendering and all six unchanged spawn guards. Rust lint, Node22/24 and delivers checks succeed. The corpus walk is test-only work, not a registration-time scan.

Clean worktree; local/GitHub heads agree and GitHub reports CLEAN. No local build, test, mutation, live registration/spawn/digest operation or cost probe. Complexity is source-derived; CI validates behavior, not live CPU/RSS or large-invalid-field latency. Security/correctness verdicts remain independent.
